overall_summary: Deduplication and recency weighting across hourly data blocks reveal a massive performance skew toward space phenomena and extreme 'What If' planetary scenarios. Videos tackling surreal planetary conditions (e.g., Venus day length, liquid diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) outpace general science or psychology shorts by 3x to 5x in views-per-day and generate significantly higher engagement ratios (likes-per-view).

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) show high velocity shortly after publication compared to older general science facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on surreal, high-stakes hypothetical scenarios involving extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (892 views) and 'This Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,026 views) demonstrate strong organic discovery and viewer retention via counter-intuitive facts.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight physics or orbital anomalies that sound fictional but are scientifically accurate.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and psychological songs-stuck-in-head shorts languish below 60-100 total views with minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard human psychology and memory tips for the time being.

weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal facts like 'Octopuses Have Three Hearts' (outside of initial spikes) have plateaued while space formats continue to compound.
weak_patterns.action: Shift biological content toward cinematic animal survival or extreme adaptations if revisited.
